questions.stem: An automated delivery drone logs a flight duration of \\(3\\) hours and \\(12\\) minutes. Express this flight duration in decimal hours.
questions.hint: Convert the minutes portion into a fraction of an hour (since there are 60 minutes in an hour) and then convert that fraction to a decimal.

steps.explain: Identify the given hours and minutes. The time is \\(3\\) hours and \\(12\\) minutes, and we need to convert the minutes to decimal hours.
Convert \\(12\\) minutes to a fraction of an hour by dividing by \\(60\\). This is because one hour contains exactly \\(60\\) minutes.
Simplify the fraction by dividing the numerator and denominator by 12. This yields a basic equivalent fraction.
Convert \\(\frac{1}{5}\\) to a decimal by dividing 1 by 5, or multiplying the terms by 2 to get tenths.
Add the decimal hours to the whole hours to find the final answer. The total duration is 3.2 hours.

questions.stem: Caitlin is training for a triathlon. On Monday she trained for 1 hour and 25 minutes. On Tuesday she trained for 2 hours and 10 minutes. On Wednesday she trained for 1 hour and 40 minutes. On Thursday she trained for 2 hours and 5 minutes. On Friday she trained for 1 hour and 55 minutes. What is the total amount of time Caitlin spent training?
questions.hint: Add the smallest units first. If you reach 60 or more, carry 1 to the next unit.

steps.explain: Write the times in columns, one column for each unit, with the SMALLEST unit on the right.

steps.explain: So the elapsed time is 4 hours 12 minutes.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Build up to whole hours, then add the minutes.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 13: Measurement

questions.stem: The following times are all on the same day. How much time has elapsed between 1535 and 1755?
questions.hint: Build up to the next whole hour, then add whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

steps.explain: Elapsed time is the time that has gone by. Build up from the start time in easy steps: first to the next whole hour, then whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

questions.stem: The following times are all on the same day. How much time has elapsed between 1047 and 1326?
questions.hint: Build up to the next whole hour, then add whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

steps.explain: Elapsed time is the time that has gone by. Build up from the start time in easy steps: first to the next whole hour, then whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

steps.explain: So the elapsed time is 6 hours 30 minutes.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Build up to whole hours, then add the minutes.

steps.explain: Add: 15 minutes + 30 minutes = 45 minutes, plus 6 hours.
The school day is 6 hours 45 minutes.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Build up to whole hours, then add the minutes.

steps.explain: Wednesday has Mathematics in two rows: 11:30 and 12:30, so it lasts from 11:30 until 1:\(30 = 2\) hours.
Add all the days.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Convert to the same unit, then divide.

steps.explain: Mathematics is 6 h. Integrated Sci/Geog/Hist is only about 4 and a half hours and The Arts about 2 hours.
English has the most hours.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

steps.explain: Each day: \(30 + 45 = 75\) minutes.
There are 5 school days.
Change minutes to hours: \(375 \div  60 = 6\) remainder 15.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Convert to the same unit, then add.
There are 60 minutes in an hour and 60 seconds in a minute.

steps.explain: Take away recess (30 min) and lunch (45 min) each day.
There are 5 days.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Convert to the same unit, then add.
There are 60 minutes in an hour and 60 seconds in a minute.

Count along the thermometer scale.
Convert to the same unit, then divide.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 13: Measurement

questions.stem: It was −3°C when Winston woke up on Friday morning. On Friday afternoon the temperature was 9°C. What was the temperature increase between Friday morning and Friday afternoon?
questions.hint: Count up to 0°C, then on to 9°C.

steps.explain: On Friday morning it was −3°C and in the afternoon 9°C. Mark them on the thermometer.

keyPoints.note: Count up or down the thermometer; mind the negatives.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 13: Measurement

questions.stem: Start at −3°C. Add on 3°C. What is the temperature?
questions.hint: Count up for a rise and down for a drop. Remember: below 0°C the numbers are negative.

steps.explain: Find the starting temperature, -3°C, on the thermometer (blue dot). Up is warmer, down is colder.

steps.explain: Why the other answers are wrong: they go the wrong way along the thermometer, or ignore the negative sign.

keyPoints.note: Count up or down the thermometer; mind the negatives.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 13: Measurement

questions.stem: Start at 7°C. Take off 11°C. What is the temperature?
questions.hint: Count up for a rise and down for a drop. Remember: below 0°C the numbers are negative.

steps.explain: Find the starting temperature, 7°C, on the thermometer (blue dot). Up is warmer, down is colder.

steps.explain: Why the other answers are wrong: they go the wrong way along the thermometer, or ignore the negative sign.

keyPoints.note: Count up or down the thermometer; mind the negatives.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 13: Measurement

questions.stem: The temperature at Mt Thredbo was −14°C. It dropped 7°C. What was the temperature then?
questions.hint: Count up for a rise and down for a drop. Remember: below 0°C the numbers are negative.

steps.explain: Find the starting temperature, -14°C, on the thermometer (blue dot). Up is warmer, down is colder.

questions.stem: When Patrick woke at 7:00 am, the temperature was 12°C. It rose by 1 degree in the first hour, 2 degrees in the second hour and 3 degrees in the third hour. The temperature continued to rise in the same pattern until 1:00 pm, when a cool change arrived. The temperature had dropped by 17 degrees by the time Patrick came home from school. What was the temperature when Patrick arrived home?
questions.hint: List the rise for each hour 7 to 1, add, then take away 17.

steps.explain: The temperature at 7:00 am was 12°C. It rose 1° in the 1st hour, 2° in the 2nd hour, 3° in the 3rd hour and so on until 1:00 pm. From 7:00 am to 1:00 pm there are 6 hours.

Add them.
The temperature at 1:00 pm was 12 + 21.
The cool change dropped the temperature by 17 degrees.

keyPoints.note: A kilogram is 1000 grams and a tonne is 1000 kilograms.
A gram is 1000 milligrams and a kilogram is 1000 grams.

questions.stem: Murray is studying for his first-aid certificate. On Monday he went to his first-aid course for 3 hours and 40 minutes. On Tuesday he studied the first-aid manual for 1 hour and 15 minutes. On Wednesday he studied the manual for 1 hour and 48 minutes. On Thursday he went to the course for 3 hours and 5 minutes. On Friday he took his first-aid exam. It went for 2 hours and 57 minutes. What was the total amount of time Murray spent getting his first-aid certificate?
questions.hint: Add the smallest units first. If you reach 60 or more, carry 1 to the next unit.

steps.explain: Write the times in columns, one column for each unit, with the SMALLEST unit on the right.

questions.stem: How much time has elapsed between 4:05 am and 7:35 am on the same day?
questions.hint: Build up to the next whole hour, then add whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

steps.explain: Elapsed time is the time that has gone by. Build up from the start time in easy steps: first to the next whole hour, then whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

questions.stem: How much time has elapsed between 7:55 pm and 8:03 pm on the same day?
questions.hint: Build up to the next whole hour, then add whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

steps.explain: Elapsed time is the time that has gone by. Build up from the start time in easy steps: first to the next whole hour, then whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

questions.stem: How much time has elapsed between 10:08 pm and 3:45 am the next day?
questions.hint: Build up to midnight, then to the end time.

steps.explain: The end time is on the NEXT day, so build up through midnight.

steps.explain: 10:08 pm → 11:00 pm is 52 minutes; 11:00 pm → 12:00 midnight is 1 hour; midnight → 3:00 am is 3 hours; 3:00 am → 3:45 am is 45 minutes.

steps.explain: So the elapsed time is 9 hours 17 minutes.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Build up to whole hours, then add the minutes.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 13: Measurement

questions.stem: How much time has elapsed between 0545 and 1355 the same day?
questions.hint: Build up to the next whole hour, then add whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

steps.explain: Elapsed time is the time that has gone by. Build up from the start time in easy steps: first to the next whole hour, then whole hours, then the leftover minutes.

Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Build up to whole hours, then add the minutes.

questions.stem: How much time has elapsed between 1256 and 1326 the next day?
questions.hint: One whole day is 24 hours.

steps.explain: The end time is on the NEXT day. The same clock time (1256) comes round again after exactly 24 hours.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 620 130" width="100%" height="auto" style="max-width:620px;display:block;margin:0 auto"><line x1="50" y1="62" x2="570" y2="62" stroke="#3b4ea8" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="50.0" cy="62" r="6" fill="#e11d1d"/><text x="50" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#1e293b">1256</text><circle cx="570.0" cy="62" r="6" fill="#e11d1d"/><text x="570" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#1e293b">1326 next day</text><path d="M50.0,56 Q310.0,14 570.0,56" fill="none" stroke="#d97706" stroke-width="3"/><text x="310" y="18" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#d97706">24 h 30 min</text></svg>

steps.explain: From 1256 today to 1256 tomorrow is 24 hours; then 1256 → 1326 is 30 minutes.

steps.explain: So 24 hours 30 minutes have elapsed.
Why the other answers are wrong: they forget to carry (60 minutes = 1 hour, 60 seconds = 1 minute), mix up hours and minutes, or add instead of subtract.

keyPoints.note: Build up to whole hours, then add the minutes.

keyPoints.note: Count up or down the thermometer; mind the negatives.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 13: Measurement

questions.stem: Calculate the new temperature after this temperature change. Start at −6°C. Take off 12°C. What is the temperature?
questions.hint: Count up for a rise and down for a drop. Remember: below 0°C the numbers are negative.

steps.explain: Find the starting temperature, -6°C, on the thermometer (blue dot). Up is warmer, down is colder.

keyPoints.note: Count up or down the thermometer; mind the negatives.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 13: Measurement

questions.stem: Calculate the new temperature after this temperature change. Start at −18°C. Add on 19°C. What is the temperature?
questions.hint: Count up for a rise and down for a drop. Remember: below 0°C the numbers are negative.

steps.explain: Find the starting temperature, -18°C, on the thermometer (blue dot). Up is warmer, down is colder.
